set.descent_text: Most parties rappel from the bolted anchor at the top of pitch 3 rather than continuing up the brushy upper pitches or onto Lovin' Arms. Every belay on the route is bolted. Double ropes allow a long rappel to the ground; with a single rope, expect more, shorter rappels.
set.rappels: Rappel from the bolted P3 anchor; double ropes make the descent quickest, a single rope needs more, shorter rappels.

climbing_route.label: South snowfield from Perfect Pass
climbing_route.notes: From camp at Perfect Pass the route heads north and up onto the broad south-side snowfield, which is the lower margin of the Whatcom Glacier. The angle is moderate and the line is obvious, aiming for the conspicuous col in the summit ridge above. Ice axe is standard and crampons are usual on firm morning snow. Because this is glacier ice under the seasonal snow, early-season parties treat it as glacier travel; later in the year the cover thins and moats open along the rock margin where the snow meets the summit block. Reports describe it as long but straightforward, roughly an hour from the pass.

climbing_route.label: Col in the summit ridge
climbing_route.notes: The snowfield is left at the obvious col on the summit ridge. Some parties instead break out onto ramps and ledges to the northeast of the col and rejoin the crest higher. The transition from snow to rock is where a moat or a lip of hard snow is most likely to be awkward, and it is worse late in the season.

climbing_route.label: South ridge crest to the summit
climbing_route.notes: The final stretch along the crest is short but very exposed, with drops on both sides. The rock here is described as poor quality and protection opportunities are limited, so a light rack and slings are carried and many parties belay this section even though the moves are only third to fourth class. The route as a whole is generally graded fourth class on account of this last bit; the scrambling itself is described as enjoyable rather than difficult, with the exposure and the loose rock being the real concerns. Descent reverses the line, and on good snow the return to Perfect Pass is very quick.

set.overview: The Douglas Glacier route climbs Mount Logan from the southeast and is rated Grade III, Class 4. It's a well-regarded, reasonably-paced 3-day objective for a fit team, approached via the Easy Pass Trail and a cross-country descent into Fisher Basin.
